B4-MLO-08-1.supports: PSI rule-of-thumb cut-offs (0.1, 0.25) and that PSI critical values depend on sample size and number of bins

B4-MLO-08-3.title: Monitoring Distributed Systems (Google SRE Book)
B4-MLO-08-3.supports: Page on symptoms, every page should be actionable, non-urgent signals belong on dashboards (principles 1, 4 and the tier table).

B4-MLO-08-4.title: scipy.stats.ks_2samp
B4-MLO-08-4.supports: The statistic is the maximum absolute difference between the empirical distribution functions of the two samples; the null hypothesis is that the distributions are identical; inputs are assumed to be drawn from a continuous distribution.

B4-MLO-08-6.title: The ML Test Score: A Rubric for ML Production Readiness and Technical Debt Reduction
B4-MLO-08-6.supports: Monitoring tests: measure whether data matches the schema and alert when it diverges significantly; alert thresholds need careful tuning to balance false positives and false negatives; models should have zero bias in aggregate and on slices.

B4-MLO-08-6.supports: PSI rule-of-thumb cut-offs (0.1, 0.25) and that PSI critical values depend on sample size and number of bins

B4-MLO-08-7.title: A critical review of existing and new population stability testing procedures in credit risk scoring
B4-MLO-08-7.supports: PSI rule-of-thumb cut-offs (0.1 small change, 0.25 substantial) are attributed in the paper to Lewis; the paper reports (citing Du Pisanie & Visagie) that the PSI critical value decreases with sample size and increases with number of groups, when group proportions are equal. It does not state the (B-1)(1/n+1/m) noise-floor formula.

B4-MLO-09-1.title: MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning (Google Cloud Architecture Center)
B4-MLO-09-1.supports: CT is a property of ML systems concerned with automatically retraining and serving models; pipeline triggers include schedule, new training data, performance degradation and changes in data distributions; data validation is required before training to decide whether to retrain and model validation occurs after training.

B4-MLO-09-2.title: Hidden Technical Debt in Machine Learning Systems
B4-MLO-09-2.supports: A model may directly influence the selection of its own future training data (direct feedback loops); action limits should be set as a sanity check and be broad enough not to trigger spuriously.

B4-MLO-09-2.title: Fighting Sampling Bias: A Framework for Training and Evaluating Credit Scoring Models
B4-MLO-09-2.supports: Outcomes of rejected applicants are unobserved; evaluating on accepted applicants overestimates scorecard performance; randomly approved loans give unbiased evaluation data; reject inference has modest potential

B4-MLO-09-3.title: MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning (Google Cloud Architecture Center)
B4-MLO-09-3.supports: CT is a property of ML systems concerned with automatically retraining and serving models; pipeline triggers include schedule, new training data, performance degradation and changes in data distributions; data validation is required before training to decide whether to retrain and model validation occurs after training.

B4-MLO-09-3.title: Hidden Technical Debt in Machine Learning Systems
B4-MLO-09-3.supports: A model may directly influence the selection of its own future training data (direct feedback loops); action limits should be set as a sanity check and be broad enough not to trigger spuriously.

B4-MLO-09-4.title: Rules of Machine Learning (Google)
B4-MLO-09-4.supports: Rule 8: know the freshness requirements of your system, i.e. how much performance degrades if the model is a day, a week or a quarter old.

B4-MLO-10-1.title: Beyond Accuracy: Behavioral Testing of NLP Models with CheckList
B4-MLO-10-1.supports: Minimum functionality, invariance and directional expectation test families

B4-MLO-10-1.title: XGBoost: Monotonic Constraints
B4-MLO-10-1.supports: Libraries can enforce monotonicity constraints so a guarantee can be built into training

B4-MLO-10-3.title: Rules of Machine Learning: Best Practices for ML Engineering (Google for Developers)
B4-MLO-10-3.supports: Rule #5 'Test getting data into the algorithm' and its advice to check that feature columns that should be populated are populated.

B4-MLO-10-3.title: Python Language Reference: Value comparisons (NaN)
B4-MLO-10-3.supports: `NaN > limit` never fails; any ordered comparison with NaN is False.

B4-MLO-10-3.title: Python built-in functions: all()
B4-MLO-10-3.supports: all([]) is True, so zero checks executed looks healthy.

B4-MLO-10-4.title: TensorFlow Data Validation: Getting started
B4-MLO-10-4.supports: Says inference uses conservative heuristics and that it is strongly advised to review the inferred schema and refine it to capture domain knowledge; skew comparators are set via thresholds in the schema.

B4-MLO-10-4.title: The ML Test Score: A Rubric for ML Production Readiness and Technical Debt Reduction (Google Research, PDF)
B4-MLO-10-4.supports: Lists 'Feature expectations are captured in a schema' (a data test) and 'Data invariants hold in training and serving inputs' (a monitoring test).

B4-MLO-11-1.title: pickle - Python object serialization (Python docs)
B4-MLO-11-1.supports: States that the pickle module is not secure, that malicious pickle data can execute arbitrary code during unpickling, that data from an untrusted or tamperable source must never be unpickled, and suggests signing data with hmac.

B4-MLO-11-1.title: Secure installs: hash-checking mode (pip docs)
B4-MLO-11-1.supports: Lock files that pin every dependency with hashes: hash-checking mode requires hashes for all requirements and dependencies and errors on any unhashed dependency.

B4-MLO-11-2.title: Rules of Machine Learning: Best Practices for ML Engineering (Google for Developers)
B4-MLO-11-2.supports: Rule #29 says the best way to make sure you train like you serve is to save the features used at serving time, and that even if you cannot do this for every example, doing it for a small fraction is useful.

B4-MLO-11-2.title: Simple Demographics Often Identify People Uniquely (Sweeney, Carnegie Mellon)
B4-MLO-11-2.supports: Date of birth plus a postal/ZIP code (with gender) is a classic quasi-identifier combination.

B4-MLO-11-2.title: Pseudonymisation (ICO, UK GDPR guidance)
B4-MLO-11-2.supports: Pseudonymised data remains personal data for whoever holds the additional information; additional information must be kept separately.

B4-MLO-11-2.title: GDPR (EUR-Lex), Recital 26
B4-MLO-11-2.supports: Recital 26: pseudonymised data that could be attributed to a person with additional information should be considered information on an identifiable natural person; data protection principles do not apply to anonymous information. (Operative articles were not readable on this page.)

B4-MLO-11-3.title: Machine Unlearning (Bourtoule et al., arXiv 1912.03817)
B4-MLO-11-3.supports: Removing one record's influence from a trained model is hard in general; research proposals such as SISA training reduce retraining cost versus retraining from scratch.

B4-MLO-11-3.title: The Secret Sharer: Evaluating and Testing Unintended Memorization in Neural Networks (Carlini et al.)
B4-MLO-11-3.supports: Rare or unique training records can be unintentionally memorised by generative sequence models, so memorisation is a factor for retention of individual records (the finding is for sequence models; the answer rightly calls it model- and data-dependent).

B4-MLO-11-4.title: Model Cards for Model Reporting (arXiv 1810.03993)
B4-MLO-11-4.supports: Abstract: model cards are short documents accompanying trained models that report benchmarked evaluation across conditions (including demographic, cultural and phenotypic groups), the intended context of use, and details of how evaluation was done.

B4-MLO-11-5.title: OWASP ML04:2023 Membership Inference Attack (correct URL)
B4-MLO-11-5.supports: Regularisation and adding noise / differential privacy are listed as prevention methods.

B4-MLO-11-5.title: Label-Only Membership Inference Attacks (Choquette-Choo et al.)
B4-MLO-11-5.supports: Label-only attacks exist and defeat defences that only hide confidence scores, so returning only a label or masking confidence does not guarantee safety.

B4-MLO-11-5.title: Membership Inference Attacks From First Principles (Carlini et al.)
B4-MLO-11-5.supports: Attacks should be evaluated at low false-positive rates, not only by average-case metrics.

B4-MLO-11-5.title: Label-Only Membership Inference Attacks (full text, Choquette-Choo et al.)
B4-MLO-11-5.supports: Query budgets of label-only attacks and that query limiting is unlikely to be a suitable defence.

B4-MLO-12-1.title: CFS Bandwidth Control (Linux kernel docs)
B4-MLO-12-1.supports: A container with a CPU limit is throttled when its quota is exhausted within a period, which can add latency in bursts; throttling counters are in cpu.stat.

B4-MLO-12-2.title: The ML Test Score: A Rubric for ML Production Readiness and Technical Debt Reduction (Google Research, PDF)
B4-MLO-12-2.supports: 'Serving models can be rolled back' is an ML Infrastructure test (Infra 7) that says rollback should be practised outside emergencies; NaN/infinity monitoring is Monitor 5 (numerical stability), not the rollback item.

B4-MLO-12-2.title: Secure installs: hash-checking mode (pip docs)
B4-MLO-12-2.supports: Lock files that pin every dependency with hashes: hash-checking mode requires hashes for all requirements and dependencies and errors on any unhashed dependency.

B4-MLO-12-3.title: tracemalloc - Trace memory allocations (Python docs)
B4-MLO-12-3.supports: The standard library's tracemalloc can compare two snapshots to find where memory grew.

B4-MLO-12-4.title: The ML Test Score: A Rubric for ML Production Readiness and Technical Debt Reduction (Google Research, PDF)
B4-MLO-12-4.supports: 'Serving models can be rolled back' is an ML Infrastructure test (Infra 7) that says rollback should be practised outside emergencies; NaN/infinity monitoring is Monitor 5 (numerical stability), not the rollback item.

B4-MLO-12-4.title: Postmortem Culture: Learning from Failure (Google SRE Book)
B4-MLO-12-4.supports: Lists on-call intervention such as release rollback or rerouting of traffic among common postmortem triggers.

B4-MLO-12-5.title: Addressing Cascading Failures (Google SRE Book)
B4-MLO-12-5.supports: Describes serving lower-quality, cheaper-to-compute results under load as graceful degradation, and warns that the code path you never use is often the one that doesn't work, recommending regular exercise of degraded paths.

B4-MLO-12-5.title: Timeouts, retries and backoff with jitter (AWS Builders' Library)

B4-MLO-12-6.title: Example Error Budget Policy (Google SRE Workbook)
B4-MLO-12-6.supports: Example policy: halt all changes and releases other than P0 issues or security fixes until the service is back within its SLO; exemptions include outages from company-wide networking problems and budget consumed by out-of-scope users; postmortem required when a single incident consumes more than 20% of the budget over four weeks.

B4-MLO-12-6.title: Embracing Risk (Google SRE Book)
B4-MLO-12-6.supports: The error budget is the difference between the SLO and measured reliability; releases may continue while budget remains and are temporarily halted when it is spent.

B4-MLO-12-6.title: Alerting on SLOs (Google SRE Workbook)
B4-MLO-12-6.supports: Burn-rate alerting over a long and a short window, as used for availability and proposed here for quality.

B4-MLO-12-7.title: Postmortem Culture: Learning from Failure (Google SRE Book)
B4-MLO-12-7.supports: Blameless postmortems assume everyone had good intentions and aim to fix systems and processes; a monitoring failure (usually manual discovery) is listed as a common postmortem trigger.

B4-MLO-12-7.title: Rules of Machine Learning: Best Practices for ML Engineering (Google for Developers)
B4-MLO-12-7.supports: Rule #10 on silent failures: a table being joined that is no longer updated; models can degrade without errors.

B4-MLO-12-9.title: Spot Instance interruption notices (Amazon EC2 User Guide)
B4-MLO-12-9.supports: Reclaimable capacity gives short, best-effort warning before interruption.

B4-MLO-12-9.title: Best practices for Amazon EC2 Spot (EC2 User Guide)
B4-MLO-12-9.supports: Spreading spot requests across instance types and Availability Zones; designing for fault tolerance.

B4-MLO-13-1.title: The ML Test Score: A Rubric for ML Production Readiness and Technical Debt Reduction (Breck et al.)
B4-MLO-13-1.supports: Lists 'Dependency changes result in notification' as a monitoring test and 'Models are tested via a canary process before they enter production serving environments' as an infrastructure test.

B4-MLO-13-1.title: Model IDs and versioning (Claude API docs)
B4-MLO-13-1.supports: Aliases are convenience pointers to the most recent snapshot; a model ID stays fixed; infrastructure around it can change; every ID has its own retirement schedule.

B4-MLO-13-2.title: MLflow Prompt Registry documentation
B4-MLO-13-2.supports: States that prompt versions in the registry are immutable once created and that an alias is a mutable named reference to a version.

B4-MLO-13-3.title: Prompt caching (OpenAI API documentation)
B4-MLO-13-3.supports: Documents that prompt caching reuses work when requests share the same prompt prefix, that the entire rendered prefix must match, and that stable content should come first with variable content such as timestamps later.

B4-MLO-14-1.title: Rules of Machine Learning (Google for Developers)
B4-MLO-14-1.supports: Rule #39 states that launch decisions are a proxy for longer-term product goals and that the metrics measurable in A/B tests are only proxies for them.

B4-MLO-14-1.title: Canarying Releases (Google SRE Workbook)
B4-MLO-14-1.supports: States the canary should be sizeable and last long enough to be representative of the overall deployment.

B4-MLO-14-2.title: Rules of Machine Learning (Google for Developers)
B4-MLO-14-2.supports: Rule #29 recommends saving the set of features used at serving time and logging them for use at training time, and notes this can be done on a small fraction of examples.

B4-MLO-14-3.title: Hidden Technical Debt in Machine Learning Systems (Sculley et al., NeurIPS 2015)
B4-MLO-14-3.supports: Section 4 states that a model may directly influence the selection of its own future training data (direct feedback loop).

B4-MLO-14-3.title: Sample ratio mismatch (Spotify Confidence glossary)
B4-MLO-14-3.supports: SRM is flagged at a strict p-value cutoff (typically 0.001) and results should not be interpreted until the imbalance is explained.

B4-MLO-14-4.title: Hidden Technical Debt in Machine Learning Systems (Sculley et al., NeurIPS 2015)
B4-MLO-14-4.supports: Section 4 states that a model may directly influence the selection of its own future training data.

B4-MLO-14-4.title: Rules of Machine Learning (Google for Developers)
B4-MLO-14-4.supports: Rule #37 discusses measuring training/serving skew, including that the same example should give the same result in training and serving and that a discrepancy probably indicates an engineering error.

B4-MLO-14-4.title: Unbiased Learning-to-Rank with Biased Feedback (PDF)
B4-MLO-14-4.supports: Position-bias propensities estimated from a small randomized swap intervention; logging ranker may be deterministic.

B4-MLO-14-5.title: Rules of Machine Learning (Google for Developers)
B4-MLO-14-5.supports: Rule #29 recommends saving the features used at serving time and logging them for training, and says that doing it for a small fraction of examples is still useful.

B4-MLO-14-5.title: The ML Test Score: A Rubric for ML Production Readiness and Technical Debt Reduction (Breck et al.)
B4-MLO-14-5.supports: Lists 'Training and serving features compute the same values' among its monitoring tests.

B4-MLO-14-6.title: Hidden Technical Debt in Machine Learning Systems (Sculley et al., NeurIPS 2015)
B4-MLO-14-6.supports: Section 7 states that the external world is rarely stable, which creates ongoing monitoring and maintenance needs.

B4-MLO-14-6.title: The ML Test Score: A Rubric for ML Production Readiness and Technical Debt Reduction (Breck et al.)
B4-MLO-14-6.supports: Presents 28 specific tests and monitoring needs, including monitoring tests for training/serving feature consistency, model staleness and prediction-quality regression.
